reason: The cited evidence (E2, E3) directly demonstrates the disorder-to-order transition via rapid heating and a 5-minute re-heat at ~1100 K for multi-element nanoparticles, supporting the core kinetic trapping and re-heating premises. E1 provides mechanistic rationale for why more elements favor single-phase formation under kinetic control, but does not directly address the re-heating window or the consequences of too-short/too-long heating, leaving those aspects inferred rather than explicitly evidenced.
premises: Rapid heating traps a disordered solid solution kinetically
A narrow re-heating window enables a disorder-to-order transition
Too short re-heating leaves insufficient mobility for ordering
Too long re-heating causes segregation, coarsening, or phase separation
The mechanism applies to >5-element noble-metal HEA nanoparticles at ~1100 K
